title: What the garrison sings
comment: One of the seven that finish the dozen (BACKLOG.md rank 8). Lore's `march-song`: the outer ward has a song about how the March War ended, in the March's tongue, and the inner ward has heard the tune across the cross-wall for forty years and has never once been told the words. Lore's `sir-roger-lestrange`: he is a Vantry man who has never learned a word of the March's tongue and does not think it a lack. Two roads, and which one the player takes is which man they asked: Gwilym has both tongues and a gate to keep (`gwilym-porter`), and Dafydd's grandfather stood on the other bank for nine years (`sentry-grandfather`).
terminalComment: BOTH ENDINGS PUT HIM BACK ON `default`, AND THAT IS A RULE AND NOT A TASTE (#693). Sir Roger's `default` lines are the only ones in npcs.json that pose `{ACCUSE}`, and `{ACCUSE}` is how the player is asked for a name. A terminal stage that left him in an errand's state would take the accusation's own prompt off the screen for the rest of the day, in the one conversation the whole day is pointed at. `validateQuestSet`'s rule 6 refuses it. The cost is that his errand has no closing lines: the toast and the journal's Done heading carry the ending instead, which is what they are for.
voiceComment: The Constable owns no dialogue state in mystery.json at all: `constable-accident` is sourced from `default` and no press moves him. So every state here is this file's, and the rule 1 check has nothing to refuse.

unasked.objective: Nobody has asked you to listen to anything.
unasked.comment: Silent until the first conversation with him, which is also the conversation the frame's `arrive` stage moves on. His fourth `default` line goes in above `{ACCUSE}` rather than under it: the token is the day's own question and stays last.

asking.objective: The garrison has a song they stop singing when the Constable comes along the walk. He wants the words before the King's inspector hears them sung. Ask somebody with the March's tongue.
asking.comment: Two men have the tongue and are in the King's pay: the porter, who keeps the gate between the two wards and both of their languages, and the sentry, whose family was on the other side of it. Either conversation answers the question; they do not answer it the same way.

englished.objective: Gwilym gave you both verses in the King's tongue, carefully, and one of them came out shorter than it went in. Take it to Sir Roger.
englished.comment: A writ and a river, and forty years of stopping when he comes along the walk. The joke Sir Roger does not quite make is that he has never once caught his own porter at it.

refused.objective: Dafydd gave you the tune and not one word of it. Tell Sir Roger, or try the other man with both tongues.
refused.comment: Dafydd stands the King's watch and keeps his opinions, and the two things have never once seemed strange to him. The porter is still a road out of here: a question carried to Gwilym after Dafydd has refused it is still a question carried.

written.objective: Sir Roger has both verses, and has decided to be a Constable who lets a song be sung over his own high table.
written.comment: Terminal, and back on `default` so the accusation's own line is on the screen again. What he does with it is nothing, which is the point: eight years of not knowing, and the answer is a river.

let-be.objective: The garrison keeps its song. Sir Roger has stopped asking, which is not the same as not wanting to know.
let-be.comment: Terminal, and back on `default` for the same reason. He takes a refusal better than he takes the answer, because a refusal is a thing he understands.
